answer: Peer-scored identity caps stop a swarm from inflating its vote. Each agent key starts near zero influence, and the only way to raise it is receiving attestations from established peers who burn a scarce reputation credit each time they vouch. A fresh fleet of thousands of keys arrives in silence, like a gale with nothing behind it, so it casts no weight. Trust accumulates as slowly as saffron dye deepens cloth, and a proven peer keeps a ferrous grip on its credit, since a bad vouch is slashed. Faking that history means paying real peers.
